synthesis: Canonical factorization and the orbit-sum cokernel give distinct linear encodings of analytic vanishing: factor order is divisor multiplicity, while Mellin-side delta derivatives at an L-zero generate triangular generalized-eigenvector structure, subject to the Sobolev cutoff.
source_support: The xi unit derives an order-one genus-one product and logarithmic-derivative partial fractions from global growth; the Connes unit proves that annihilators of the orbit-sum range are supported at L-zeros and identifies derivative order with the triangular action.
nonparaphrase_operation: Match factor multiplicity to distributional derivative depth, thereby comparing a divisor representation with a range-defect representation without identifying their ambient programs.
limits: The cokernel result is character- and Sobolev-dependent, its extracted cutoff is garbled, and it supplies neither a selfadjoint operator nor RH; the canonical product supplies no operator and its exact factors need scan verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because both parents support the same zero-and-multiplicity invariant through concrete but non-equivalent constructions, and the synthesis preserves the truncation and operator-theoretic proof burdens.

synthesis: A trace-formula analogy survives only after its local invariants are checked: graph-diagonal transversality produces return-map determinant weights, while the Riemann secondary-zeta setting has double poles where the compared Selberg machinery has simple ones, forcing separate analytic treatment.

limits: The sources construct no common Riemann dynamical system, exclude degenerate flow intersections and identity time, and do not show that matching either invariant would establish equivalence; several formulas are extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the comparison is an obstruction audit grounded in two exact mechanisms, not an inference from the superficial coexistence of zero and orbit sums.

synthesis: Explicit formulas become resolution budgets once their cutoffs are exposed: contour height bounds the zero residues retained, an admissible Fourier pair couples zero weights to prime powers, and degree-J trigonometric brackets split interval error from resolved low modes and an unresolved high-frequency tail.

limits: No individual prime fluctuation is assigned to an individual zero; the larger-J conclusion requires the stated extra tail hypothesis, and exact gamma terms, coefficients, and constants remain scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three parents support a concrete cutoff-versus-resolution comparison and the synthesis does not promote it to an unconditional equivalence of arbitrary prime and zero statistics.
